extractor_seam.seam_derivation: traced directly from source, not assumed: ConsumeReleaseArgs calls ConsumesParam, which recurses through first-party callees; CallReleasesReceiver is the extension-method-receiver twin of the same call; EmitFlowExpr is the ONE place that materializes ConsumeReleaseArgs's answer into an unconditional `release` op (Program.cs ~4485-4488) AND the ONE place whose 'consumed' set suppresses the matching `use` op for the same statement. B1-F2-F2 authorized ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam/CallReleasesReceiver alongside EmitFlowExpr for a two-role design; B1-F2-F3a/F3a-R1/F3b (see b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture below) replaced that design with uniform delegation, which reads or reasons about a callee's guard shape from the extractor side NEVER, not just narrowly -- so ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam/CallReleasesReceiver's tracking-facing answer is never touched again, and B1-F2-F4 re-freezes all three. DisposesLocal, ParameterIsStable and BuildGuardedFacts stay FROZEN throughout, as always.
extractor_seam.authorized_change_shape: ONE ROLE, uniform, unconditional (B1-F2-F4, correcting B1-F2-F2's two-role design -- see b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture for the full finding and why the two-role design could not be completed): EmitFlowExpr turns EVERY ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam-derived `release` op into a `use` op for the same local at the same call-site statement line, with no exception and no guard inspection of any kind -- never a guard-eligibility test, never a partial/conditional cut, never Election/Cells/Transform/fixpoint math inside Roslyn (that math stays exactly where B1 already froze it: rust/crates/own-bridge/, policed by production_diff_gate.rust). ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam/CallReleasesReceiver's own answers are read but never rewritten by this change, so the escape/tracking admission check at Program.cs's consumedArg keeps seeing exactly what it sees today -- b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.finding_a's failure mode (7 of 8 canonical fixtures losing all tracking) cannot recur, because nothing about tracking's own input changes at all. Making ConsumesParam path-sensitive remains explicitly NOT authorized, as before.

b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.task: B1-F2-F2: a second zero-semantics seam freeze, correcting the mechanical mismatch B1-F2's own boundary still had once the concrete B2.1a implementation was actually derived -- before any production byte changed
b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.finding_a: ConsumeReleaseArgs's return value drives TWO independent decisions today: EmitFlowExpr's release fabrication (Program.cs ~4485-4488) AND the escape-check's tracking admission (Program.cs ~7380-7384, `consumedArg`). PROVEN by direct measurement (not assumed): a scratch, never-committed edit forcing ConsumeReleaseArgs to always answer 'nothing consumed' was run against all 8 named acceptance fixtures (own-check.sh --emit-facts, before/after facts.json diffed byte-for-byte) plus the full corpus/p036-bakeoff (12 files) and corpus/p037-shapes (55 files) populations. Result: 7 of 8 canonical fixtures' caller method (Leak/Use) disappeared from functions[] entirely and reappeared as a body-less guarded_functions[] orphan (ALL acquire/release/use provenance for the local gone, not just the fabricated release); the 8th (gv4-control-aliased-self-null) stayed in functions[] but lost ALL tracking of its local `s`, including its own SEPARATE, HONEST, unconditional `s.Dispose()` three lines later -- the false OWN003 that fixture exists to witness went from 1 finding to 0, for the wrong reason (the local vanished from analysis, not because the guarded call was correctly reasoned about). Across the two full populations: 9 functions newly orphaned, 4 more with a changed body, out of 94 functions[] records total (~14%); 0 new findings, 3 findings lost (all false-positive OWN003s disappearing by the same erasure, not by correct reasoning). ANSWER: the existing 3-method seam is NOT implementable without destroying caller obligation tracking -- NO.
b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.finding_a_scratch_diff: scripts/p037_b_extractor_diff_gate.py's own selftest and this record's own production_diff_gate.extractor prove no committed byte of Program.cs changed for this investigation; the edit was a single early `return new List<string>();` in ConsumeReleaseArgs, reverted via `git checkout` immediately after each measurement pass, working tree confirmed clean before, between and after every pass.
b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.finding_b: the emitted guarded_facts sidecar is insufficient as the ONLY abstention signal, because G-V4 deliberately emits NOTHING for a rejected guard candidate (Program.cs ~3349-3356: `if (!typeFits || !Stable(gp)) continue; // not eligible: no entry, by design`) -- confirmed directly on the real gv4-control-aliased-self-null fixture: Close's own functions[] record carries NO guarded_facts key at all (not even an empty one), identical in shape to a genuinely unguarded method, so a rule of the form 'abstain when the callee's guards[] is non-empty' cannot distinguish the two and would leave the fabricated release (and the false OWN003) exactly as today's B1 record already measured. The raw guard-CANDIDATE shape-match (Program.cs ~3315-3348, an OwnParam + truth/is_null/not_null predicate test against an if-condition, BEFORE the typeFits/Stable eligibility gate) is the one thing that would cover both eligible and rejected cases uniformly, but it exists ONLY as inline logic inside BuildGuardedFacts's own loop today, not as a separately callable helper -- extracting it (a semantics-preserving refactor: BuildGuardedFacts's OWN emitted guarded_facts must stay byte-identical, only the internal structure changes) is the likely resolution, but is NOT proven by a scratch measurement in this task the way finding_a is, and is therefore NOT authorized into mutable_methods here. Making ConsumesParam recompute guard eligibility independently (a second recognizer) remains forbidden regardless.
b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.finding_c: difference_policy.note and first_semantic_hypothesis (pre-B1-F2-F2) referenced a first_semantic_hypothesis.facts_expectation field that did not exist, while still asserting the stale pre-treatment claim 'unchanged, full stop' -- corrected by first_semantic_hypothesis.facts_expectation (below) and difference_policy.note (corrected in place).
b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.hostile_control_broad_retirement: scratch, never-committed measurement of the OPPOSITE extreme (section 10's hostile alternative): the same forced-empty ConsumeReleaseArgs edit IS the broad-retirement experiment (it stops emitting a legacy release for every first-party consumer call the sidecar would represent, not just guard-territory ones) -- the finding_a numbers above ARE this measurement. Additionally measured against corpus/real-world (66 files) and corpus/wpf (56 files): ZERO functions[] or finding changes in either -- the mechanism is completely inert outside the guarded-consume call shape, so the blast radius is confined to the P-037-relevant population, but WITHIN that population (67 files, p036-bakeoff + p037-shapes) it reaches 9 orphaned + 4 corrupted functions out of 94 (~14%), not a handful of hand-picked fixtures. VERDICT: REJECTED -- not narrow within the population it actually touches, and its apparent verdict-level 'improvement' (3 false positives disappearing, 0 new ones) is coincidental erasure, not correct reasoning, and would identically mask a REAL leak sharing the same shape.
b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.chosen_direction_not_yet_implemented: SUPERSEDED by b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture below (B1-F2-F3a/F3a-R1/F3b); recorded here unedited because it is what B1-F2-F2 actually concluded, not because it is still the plan. b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.task: B1-F2-F3a / B1-F2-F3a-R1 / B1-F2-F3b: replacing b1_f2_f2_seam_investigation.chosen_direction_not_yet_implemented's two-role guard-territory-abstention design, after its own finding_b proved a sidecar-only abstention test cannot cover G-V4-rejected guards (they carry no guarded_facts entry at all, 'not eligible: no entry, by design')
b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.experiment_a: an isolated measurement (ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam held byte-identical; ONLY EmitFlowExpr's treatment of the already-computed consumed set changed, release to use) over the 8 named acceptance fixtures, the full corpus/{real-world,wpf,di,fixtures,p036-bakeoff,p037-shapes} population and the repo tree. B1-F2-F3a-R1 corrected a batched-Roslyn-compilation bug in the investigation's OWN scratch tooling (corpus/p036-bakeoff has duplicate, unnamespaced top-level class names across a fixture's before.cs/after.cs pair; batching them into one compilation corrupts symbol resolution) -- the governed scripts/p037_mos_snapshot.py and scripts/p037_verdict_snapshot.py were never affected, only ad hoc investigation scripts that batched a whole directory. Result: admission/tracking are provably unaffected by the release-to-use conversion itself; the fabricated release's disappearance as a leak on real, uncontrolled populations is an EXPECTED, INTERMEDIATE B2.1a-alone regression (a real leak becomes temporarily invisible to BOTH engines equally, since both read the same raw facts) that B2.1b/c's Rust solver resolves, not a defect in the cut.
b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.rust_obligations: the pattern classes B2.1b/c's Rust solver must resolve, derived from Experiment A's own ground-truth-checked movements: unconditional (restore consume), guarded-literal-true (a real leak: restore consume, OWN001), guarded-literal-false (restore consume, no finding), guarded-opaque (restore consume, OWN051 -- a G-V4-mutated wrapper argument is already marked kind=opaque by the existing frozen Classify/Stable() logic, no extractor change needed for that shape), eligible-early-return (restore consume via a flow-sensitive summary recognizing early-return-then-dispose from already-emitted body ops), wrapper-id/wrapper-neg (an edge import via the kind=param argument binding -- id/neg transform, per corpus/p037-shapes/guard-forward-negated and the wrapper-forward/negation-wrapper canonical fixtures), class-3/unresolved-else (join of must+unknown collapsing to unknown, using the already-emitted guard+call facts on the caller's own body -- the F1 pin's own shape).
b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.rejected_alternatives: (1) a narrow 'rejected-guard recognizer' veto inside EmitFlowExpr, factoring BuildGuardedFacts's condition-match logic into a shared, single-source recognizer proven byte-identical for BuildGuardedFacts's own output: exact causal tracing against corrected, isolated per-file measurements showed it fixes only 1 of 3 named G-V4 controls (the two wrapper-shaped controls need the Outer->Inner forwarding boundary crossed, which the veto never inspects), never covers early-return, and leaves class-3 untouched -- confirming finding_b rather than resolving it. (2) a broader emitter-only retirement dropping the release op instead of degrading it: re-measured and REJECTED for the same reason finding_a already found -- it destroys caller tracking, not just release fabrication.
b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.delegation_closure_claim: the HYPOTHESIS this architecture rests on: for EVERY raw release whose provenance is EmitFlowExpr <- ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam, over the FULL frozen population (both functions[].guarded_facts and guarded_functions[].guarded_facts, both kind=var and kind=param argument identity forms), there exists exactly one corresponding, already-emitted guarded_facts.calls[] entry on the SAME caller at the SAME call-site statement line -- first measured by a scratch, never-committed prototype (40/40, 0 missing, 0 ambiguous) and ACCEPTED AS INVESTIGATION only, since the prototype's artifacts were never committed and the count was not independently reproducible from the repository. B1-F2-F4 replaced it with scripts/p037_delegation_closure.py (see b1_f2_f4_findings.delegation_closure_tool), a committed, governed control independently reproducing the same 40/40 CORRELATION count mechanically from the UNMODIFIED extractor. CORRECTED by B1-F2-F4-R1 (see b1_f2_f4_r1_findings.delegation_closure_claim_corrected): neither the scratch prototype nor the committed tool PROVES this hypothesis exhaustively -- a release op carries no provenance tag, so a genuinely direct dispose sharing its statement line with an unrelated, eligible, same-variable call is structurally indistinguishable from a call-fabricated one, and would be counted as a correlation match by either tool. The hypothesis is strongly CORROBORATED (40/40, independently reproduced, zero missing/ambiguous), never exhaustively PROVEN, by either measurement; the true changed-site population is established, once, by the governed before/after raw-fact diff first_semantic_hypothesis.facts_expectation.verified_by now requires at B2.1a itself.
b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.architecture_accepted: Extractor: retains tracking, emits honest call facts, NEVER turns the legacy first-party may-consume inference into an unconditional caller-side release -- uniformly, not just in guard territory. Rust: sole Phase-B authority deciding interprocedural consume, reading the ALREADY-EMITTED guarded_facts.calls[]/guards[] sidecar (frozen note §10.3: 'A2.2 emits honest facts for every relevant call, including calls the legacy ConsumesParam path currently classifies as consuming'). Consequence: treatment.extractor_seam.mutable_methods narrows from four methods back to EmitFlowExpr alone, and scripts/p037_b_extractor_diff_gate.py's MUTABLE_METHODS narrows to match (B1-F2-F4).

blocker_a.fix: _measure()/compare()/verify() are epoch-aware: epoch a2d keeps its existing zero-parity-divergence semantics byte-for-byte; epoch b captures a divergence, derives a structured witness from the captured MOS/guarded-fact data, classifies it via scripts/p037_b_classifier.py, and accepts the snapshot as evidence only when every divergence classifies into APPLICATION_REFINEMENT/SUMMARY_REFINEMENT/LEGACY_HONESTY -- an UNCLASSIFIED divergence, or any divergence at all on epoch a2d, still fails the snapshot.

b1_f2_f4_findings.classifier_gap_closed: scripts/p037_b_classifier.py's GAP_REAL_WITNESS_SOURCE (contract-complete, tested only against synthetic witnesses) is closed by a real witness-derivation adapter reading captured MOS/guarded-fact/call-site data structurally -- never a fixture filename, directory name, diagnostic code, or handwritten allowlist. The classifier's own class rules and synthetic selftest are unchanged; this is additional input plumbing, proven today (pre-treatment) to correctly derive zero divergent witnesses over the unchanged population -- the same 'contract-complete, not yet exercised on a real difference' honesty the classifier's own module docstring already states, now true one layer further out.
b1_f2_f4_findings.rollback_contract: Phase-B after-evidence distinguishes: on the UNAFFECTED sample, Python stays exact against the frozen rollback/reference expectation; on the P-037 TREATMENT SLICE, Python may intentionally differ from Rust, every difference recorded and classified, with no requirement that Python ever implement guarded summaries. 'Rollback still works' is never conflated with 'rollback produces new Rust semantics'.

b1_f2_f4_r1_findings.task: B1-F2-F4-R1: a narrow corrective task, held BEFORE any R_B retake, after independent owner review of the B1-F2-F4 head found three defects in the instrument itself (not in production code -- zero production semantics moved by this task either).
b1_f2_f4_r1_findings.before_after_mos_compare_corrected: scripts/p037_mos_snapshot.py's compare() computed its OWN before/after MOS movement (moved[python]/moved[rust]) via bare, epoch-blind inequality, even though _measure()/divergence_status() were already correctly epoch-aware for intra-after (Python-vs-Rust) divergence. A real R_B-vs-B_after comparison would therefore have reported MOVED/failure the instant Rust's own MOS legitimately changed under treatment, regardless of whether every last byte of that change was classified -- making the epoch-b classification work already done pointless for the one comparison it actually has to survive. Fixed: compare()'s before/after loop (factored into the new, directly unit-tested _compare_documents()) now applies divergence_status()/explain_divergence() to the Rust axis too, treating before-Rust as the reference ('legacy') role and after-Rust as the value a guarded field must justify -- the SAME whole-document classifier discipline already required for intra-after divergence, reused rather than duplicated (p037_b_classifier.py's derive_document_witnesses()/explain_divergence() parameters were renamed legacy_doc/new_doc, generically, for this reuse). The Python axis, being the legacy/reference/rollback engine, gets a DIFFERENT rule: its own before/after movement is accepted only as a direct mechanical consequence of the raw facts hash ALSO moving on the same document, never independently and never merely because Rust is expected to move -- epoch a2d keeps the original, unconditional zero-movement policy for both axes throughout, exactly as before. Three new selftest scenarios prove it: a classified Rust refinement passes under epoch b and fails identically under epoch a2d; the same movement with no guarded field fails under epoch b; a classified movement riding alongside an unrelated residual difference (unresolved[] gaining an entry) still fails.
b1_f2_f4_r1_findings.delegation_closure_claim_corrected: scripts/p037_delegation_closure.py's module docstring, and this record's own b1_f2_f3b_delegation_architecture.delegation_closure_claim/b1_f2_f4_findings.delegation_closure_tool, stated the tool's 40/40 result as though it PROVED that every raw release fabricated by the legacy interprocedural shortcut has a corresponding sidecar call fact -- an overclaim: a release op carries only {var, line}, no provenance tag, so a genuinely direct dispose (never touched by ConsumeReleaseArgs/ConsumesParam at all) that happens to share its statement line with an unrelated, ELIGIBLE, same-variable call (`s.Dispose(); Take(s);` on one physical line) is structurally INDISTINGUISHABLE from a call-fabricated release, and the tool reports it 'covered' either way. The 40/40 count is real, independently reproducible, and strongly corroborates the hypothesis -- it does not, and structurally cannot, prove it exhaustively without either (a) an isolated, materialized counterfactual extraction (mutating a DETACHED copy of the extractor to turn fabricated releases into uses and computing an exact delta -- never patching the governed working tree, never duplicating ConsumeReleaseArgs's semantics in Python), deliberately NOT built by this task, or (b) the governed before/after raw-fact diff B2.1a's own landing already requires (first_semantic_hypothesis.facts_expectation.verified_by, corrected by this same task).
